defect_observations.observation: Route drivers changed since the packet was built: handbook/parts/p15.tex now hashes 2c6f3003... (packet 9B7AC188...) and handbook/annex/p15.tex now hashes f05d881f... (packet A395BEA5...). The chapter and its annex are still input (parts/p15.tex:42, annex/p15.tex:41); body and annex file hashes match the queue.

The annex displays only the exact-sigma roulette threshold 19/sqrt(360); the sigma-replaced-by-one threshold 361*(1/19)/sqrt(361)=1 behind the body's 0.1587 is left to the reader. The body (lines 109-112) calls 1-Phi(19/sqrt 360) 'the source approximation', whereas the source (PDF p.153) evaluates only P(chi>=1)=0.1587 after replacing sigma by 1; both values are present, so the source variant is preserved.

Source Example 3.4.7 (PDF p.154) also illustrates the histogram correction with P(S_16<=11) read as P(S_16<=11.5) and motivates it by complement consistency; the handbook states only the general rule.
The pointwise bound |X_1-X'_1|>=|X_1|/2 on {|X_1|>2M, |X'_1|<=M} and the finiteness of E(X_1^2;|X_1|<=2M) behind EY_1^2 >= (p/4)E(X_1^2;|X_1|>2M)=infinity are left implicit.
The random-index theorem delivers the normalizer sigma*sqrt(floor(t/mu)); the passage to sigma*sqrt(t/mu) (a deterministic factor tending to one, covered by the perturbation lemma) is not written.

The unique-factorization premise asserts that the Euclidean algorithm's last nonzero remainder is the gcd without showing it divides both inputs; this is a supporting arithmetic premise, not the promised reciprocal-sum argument, which is complete.
The chapter cites Section 3.4 at pp.144-161; the section heading and one introductory sentence sit at the foot of printed p.143 (PDF p.151). No substantive content is on p.143.

The boundary lists the Heyde remark among separate presentations but does not mention the same remark block's van Beek (1972) constant 0.8 and Hall (1982) pointers (PDF p.157); these are literature remarks, not source results.
